text:
emily: heads up — running into a subtle async bug with the Python SDK + httpx. When the SDK creates the AsyncClient synchronously in __init__, it seems to bind to the current loop and then tests using pytest-asyncio/uvloop fail with "Task attached to a different loop" or hangs on shutdown. repro below

emily: minimal-ish snippet i used:
```py
# top-level sync creation (this is what our SDK does today)
client = RedwoodAsyncClient()

async def test_call():
    await client.generate(text="hello")

# pytest-asyncio runs test_call inside its event loop
```

emily: error i get when running under pytest-asyncio + uvloop:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/.../site-packages/httpcore/_async/base.py", line 89, in some_dispatch
RuntimeError: Task <Task pending name='Task-5' ...> got Future attached to a different loop
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
Task was destroyed but it is pending!
```

emily: quick workaround is to create the AsyncClient inside the async test or call client.init_async(loop=asyncio.get_running_loop()) before using, but that defeats the point of having a shared client. anyone seen this?

dan: yeah this is a classic loop-affinity issue. if the AsyncClient is constructed in sync code before any loop exists or in a different loop, its internal httpcore/httpx objects can be tied to that loop. creating it lazily inside the running loop is safest.

alex: can you paste the SDK version + httpx/httpcore versions? we changed how we instantiate the transport in 0.8.x that might be related.

emily: sdk 0.8.3, httpx 0.23.3, httpcore 0.16.3. repro is 1) import SDK at module top-level, 2) run pytest -q with pytest-asyncio plugin + uvloop.

dan: we should avoid creating any AsyncClient in __init__ on the sync path. plan options: 1) lazy-init per-event-loop (cache by loop id), 2) require explicit async init (async factory), or 3) create a sync wrapper that proxies to an async client created on first use.

alex: +1 on lazy per-loop cache. also watch out for contextvars propagation if tasks cross loops.

emily: opened a quick repro in a gist and a minimal pytest repo. also filed a GH issue with reproduction and stack trace. linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/2345

ci-bot: Created issue #2345 (redwood-inference/python-sdk) for "AsyncClient created synchronously causes loop affinity/pytest-asyncio failures" — assigned to @dan. :white_check_mark:

dan: thanks, i'll take a look. immediate quick-fix in code: change constructor to not instantiate httpx.AsyncClient, add _get_async_client(self) that does:
```py
async def _get_async_client(self):
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    if loop not in self._client_by_loop:
        self._client_by_loop[loop] = httpx.AsyncClient(**opts)
    return self._client_by_loop[loop]
```

dan: this keeps a client per loop and avoids cross-loop futures. we should add a clear on close and tests that use pytest-asyncio/uvloop in CI matrix.

emily: confirmed the lazy approach fixes my pytest failure locally. thanks! :tada:

alex: we should also add a note in the SDK docs about not creating client instances at import time if you expect to use them in multiple async runtimes or test frameworks.

emily: filed a follow-up PR doc update and a small unit test. will follow up on GH issue with the PR link.

ci-bot: PR #2360 opened by @emily: "Fix: lazy init AsyncClient per event loop" — running CI.
